question: Can the learning rate be set automatically, with no search, by estimating a running lower bound on the distance D=||x0-x*|| to the solution, with optimal convex rates and tuned-baseline performance in deep learning?
hypothesis: With d0 <= D, final loss should be independent of the choice of d0 (tested in Sec 7.10).
contributions: D-Adaptation: first hyper-parameter-free method for convex Lipschitz functions with the optimal rate and no multiplicative log factors (asymptotic)
SGD and Adam variants (Algorithms 4, 5) tested on more than a dozen problems

method.summary: Maintains d_k, a non-decreasing lower bound on D built from dual-averaging quantities (d_hat from sum of gradient-step inner products), and uses d_k as the LR scale. SGD (Alg 4) and Adam (Alg 5) variants take a user schedule gamma_k (base 1.0) and are run against hand-tuned baselines.
method.task: learning-rate-free optimisation; convex logistic regression and deep-learning benchmarks (vision, NLP, MRI, recommendation)

limits: Theory covers only convex Lipschitz, deterministic subgradient; SGD/Adam variants have no theory (Sec 6, 4.2).
Theorem 1 is asymptotic; for fixed n a worst-case function depends on d0 (Thm 2 pays log2(D/d0)).
Requires d0 <= D; returns a weighted average iterate, not last iterate.
ViT underperforms and the cause is unresolved ('may explain').
COCO needed retuned weight decay; baseline LR tuning granularity unknown.
COCOB comparison confounded by schedule/warmup support.
Largest model RoBERTa 110M; no large-scale LLM runs.
No code or seeds for COCO stated; logistic regression reports training accuracy only.

Appendix A.1: Theorem 1 holds only for n beyond instance-dependent thresholds (n_hat where d_k >= d_{n+1}/2, and r where ||g_n||^2 <= sum of previous ||g||^2), neither quantified, so no finite-n guarantee.
Theorem 1 proof assumes ||g_k|| <= G and g0 != 0 (g0=0 trivial); the step size in Alg 1 uses 1/||g0|| for gamma_0 and no G.
Appendix A.2 proof only needs the G^2-free step at the cost of the extra term 8DG^2 log2+(D/d0)/((n+1)||g0||) (as printed in main text too).
The proof of Theorem 1 prints constant 16 before Jensen and 12 after, an internal inconsistency in constants.
Theorem 4 requires the AdaGrad matrices to be monotone and a bound G on coordinates; Algorithm 3 uses G∞ in a_0.

Adam derivation (App F) treats quantities 1-D, drops momentum (beta1=0), and the implemented Adam step is the non-dual-averaging step, which authors note 'is the only way currently supported by our theory' for the DA form only; the shipped Adam variant is not covered.
